na: مقطع وادي البيح للعصرين البرمي والترياسي
s: Carbonate section that recorded ocean acidification during the greatest mass extinction
el: pH fall of up to 0.7 over about 10,000 years
te: Where the ancient sea turned sour
se: Rocks in Wadi Bih show that the sea became more acidic during the worst extinction in Earth's history, about 252 million years ago
sa: تكشف صخور وادي البيح أن مياه البحر ازدادت حموضة في أثناء أسوأ انقراض جماعي عرفته الأرض قبل نحو 252 مليون سنة
desc: Wadi Bih in the Musandam Mountains of Ras Al Khaimah exposes a shallow-marine carbonate succession laid down on a wide platform connected to the Neo-Tethys Ocean. Boron isotopes from this section stepped up from about 10.9‰ to 15.3‰ at about 252.04 Ma, then fell to about 8.2‰, which Clarkson et al. (2015) calculate as a pH drop of up to 0.7. The acidification event began near 251.88 Ma, lasted about 10,000 years and coincides with the second pulse of the Permo-Triassic mass extinction. The authors link it to the preferential loss of heavily calcified marine life.
sig: Boron isotopes from this UAE section are key evidence that ocean acidification helped drive the Permo-Triassic mass extinction.
refs: Clarkson, M.O., Kasemann, S.A., Wood, R.A., Lenton, T.M., Daines, S.J., Richoz, S., Ohnemueller, F., Meixner, A., Poulton, S.W. & Tipper, E.T. (2015). Ocean acidification and the Permo-Triassic mass extinction. Science 348(6231), 229–232. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa0193
Clarkson, M.O. et al. (2015). (Table S1) Boron, carbon and oxygen isotope data from Wadi Bih, United Arab Emirates. PANGAEA. https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.845819
conf: Coordinates are the Wadi_Bih event in the PANGAEA dataset (25.842, 56.11158). Timeline spans the two dated events in the source (about 252.04 Ma and 251.88 Ma), not the whole section. Arabic name is a descriptive translation.

na: مقطع وادي النقب عند الحد بين العصرين الترياسي والجوراسي
s: Equatorial carbonate ramp that crossed the end-Triassic extinction
dr: Ghalilah Formation to basal Musandam Limestone; boundary about 201.3 Ma
te: A reef sea at the edge of an extinction
se: In Wadi Naqab, layers of ancient sea floor run straight through the end-Triassic extinction, about 201 million years ago
sa: في وادي النقب تمتد طبقات من قاع بحر قديم عبر الانقراض الذي ختم العصر الترياسي قبل نحو 201 مليون سنة
desc: Wadi Naqab in Ras Al Khaimah is one of four logged sections of an equatorial mixed carbonate–siliciclastic ramp on the Musandam Peninsula. The Ghalilah Formation here includes a Sakhra Member oolite about 26 m thick and a Shuba Member about 50 m thick, followed by a 7 m cross-bedded ooid grainstone at the base of the Musandam Limestone. Hönig et al. (2017) place the Triassic–Jurassic boundary at the Shuba–Musandam transition using strontium isotope ages, carbon isotopes and fossils, and tentatively record a positive carbon-isotope shift of about 3.5–4‰. They found no clear evidence of a biocalcification crisis at the boundary.
sig: A rare shallow tropical record of the end-Triassic mass extinction, used to test whether ocean acidification struck reef-building life.
refs: Hönig, M.R., John, C.M. & Manning, C. (2017). Development of an equatorial carbonate platform across the Triassic–Jurassic boundary and links to global palaeoenvironmental changes (Musandam Peninsula, UAE/Oman). Gondwana Research, 100–117. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2016.11.007
conf: Coordinates are the log base given by Hönig et al. (N 25°43′5.7″, E 56°05′14.1″). Timeline runs from the maximum brachiopod age at the top of the Asfal Member (about 208.3 Ma) to the boundary age used (about 201.3 Ma). Arabic name is a descriptive translation.

s: Late Triassic shallow-sea limestones of the Ghalilah Formation
dr: Ghalilah Formation (Asfal, Sumra, Sakhra and Shuba members)
te: A tropical sea in the mountains
se: The cliffs of Wadi Ghalilah were once a warm sea near the equator, full of shells and reefs
sa: كانت منحدرات وادي غليلة يومًا بحرًا دافئًا قرب خط الاستواء يعجّ بالأصداف والشعاب
desc: Wadi Ghalilah in northern Ras Al Khaimah is a logged section of the Ghalilah Formation, which records a shallow equatorial carbonate ramp on the Musandam Peninsula. The formation is divided into the Asfal, Sumra, Sakhra and Shuba members; the Asfal Member was deposited after about 232 Ma and the Shuba Member is about 60 m thick at this section. Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016) describe the Ghalilah Formation as a complete, continuous shallow-water carbonate sequence from the Upper Triassic into the Lower Jurassic, with a negative carbon-isotope excursion reaching about –2.8‰ just below the boundary. Their data point to aragonite supersaturation, rather than acidification, at the Triassic–Jurassic boundary.
sig: A continuous equatorial shallow-water record of the Late Triassic and the end-Triassic extinction, where many higher-latitude sections have gaps.
ex: Hönig et al. (2017); Al-Suwaidi et al. (2016)
disc: Four members: Asfal, Sumra, Sakhra, Shuba
refs: Hönig, M.R., John, C.M. & Manning, C. (2017). Development of an equatorial carbonate platform across the Triassic–Jurassic boundary and links to global palaeoenvironmental changes (Musandam Peninsula, UAE/Oman). Gondwana Research, 100–117. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2016.11.007

Al-Suwaidi, A.H., Steuber, T. & Suarez, M.B. (2016). The Triassic–Jurassic boundary event from an equatorial carbonate platform (Ghalilah Formation, United Arab Emirates). Journal of the Geological Society. https://doi.org/10.1144/jgs2015-102
conf: Coordinates are the Wadi Ghalilah log base given by Hönig et al. (N 25°58′23.1″, E 56°05′40.5″). Al-Suwaidi et al. describe the formation as a whole; the source does not say their samples came from this exact section. Timeline runs from about 232 Ma (after which the Asfal Member was deposited) to the boundary age used (about 201.3 Ma).

s: Pale granite dykes cutting the Semail ophiolite mantle on the Fujairah coast
dr: Leucogranite and tonalite dykes, about 92.4–91.0 Ma
te: White granite in the dark mantle
se: At Ras Dadnah, white granite veins slice through dark rocks that once lay deep beneath the ocean floor
sa: في رأس ضدنا تشقّ عروق من الجرانيت الأبيض صخورًا داكنة كانت يومًا في أعماق ما تحت قاع المحيط
desc: Ras Dadnah on the Fujairah coast exposes felsic dykes and sills that intrude mantle rocks of the Semail ophiolite. Rioux et al. (2021) dated a tourmaline–garnet leucogranite here at 92.361 ± 0.026 Ma, a biotite tonalite from a composite sill at 91.292 ± 0.061 Ma and a tonalite west of Ras Dadnah at 90.998 ± 0.052 Ma. These ages are younger than the main ophiolite crust and are used to study melting during subduction initiation. In a 2024 geoheritage evaluation, the Ras Dadnah leucogranite outcrop ranked highest of the Fujairah sites for scientific value.
sig: A rare, easily reached exposure of granite formed inside an ophiolite mantle, dated to within tens of thousands of years.
ex: Rioux et al. (2021); Sayama et al. (2024)
refs: Rioux, M., Garber, J.M., Searle, M., Kelemen, P., Miyashita, S., Adachi, Y. & Bowring, S. (2021). High-precision U-Pb zircon dating of late magmatism in the Samail ophiolite: A record of subduction initiation. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 126, e2020JB020758. https://doi.org/10.1029/2020JB020758

Sayama, K., Parker, A.G., Parton, A. & Viles, H. (2024). Reflecting Experiences of Regional Academic, Tourism, and Education Specialists in Geoheritage Evaluation for Fujairah, UAE and Southeast Arabia. Geoheritage 16, 90. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12371-024-00995-1
conf: No published outcrop coordinate was found; coordinates are those of Dadna village (25°31′21″N, 56°21′20″E, gazetteer/Wikipedia), so the outcrop position is approximate. Arabic name ضدنا follows the Arabic spelling of the village.

s: Mingled dark and pale magmas of the Semail ophiolite's late crust
se: Near Fujairah, dark and light rocks swirl together like oil and vinegar, frozen from two magmas that met underground
sa: قرب الفجيرة تتداخل صخور داكنة وأخرى فاتحة كالزيت والخل، تجمّدت من صهارتين التقتا في باطن الأرض
desc: West of Fujairah city the ophiolite crust contains intrusions of the Fujairah facies, where dark gabbro and pale tonalite are mingled in so-called vinaigrette textures. Goodenough et al. (2010) dated the felsic part of one such intrusion at 95.26 ± 0.31 Ma. They showed that this later magmatic sequence formed over about 1.2 million years, between about 96.40 and 95.26 Ma, and that obduction began around 94.5 Ma. Rioux et al. (2021) also dated Fujairah gabbro and tonalites from the Aswad block.
sig: Key evidence that the Oman–UAE ophiolite crust was built in more than one magmatic phase just before it was thrust onto Arabia.
disc: Late magmatism lasted about 1.2 million years
refs: Goodenough, K.M., Styles, M.T., Schofield, D., Thomas, R.J., Crowley, Q.C., Lilly, R.M., McKervey, J., Stephenson, D. & Carney, J.N. (2010). Architecture of the Oman–UAE ophiolite: evidence for a multi-phase magmatic history. Arabian Journal of Geosciences 3(4), 439–458. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12517-010-0177-3

Rioux, M., Garber, J.M., Searle, M., Kelemen, P., Miyashita, S., Adachi, Y. & Bowring, S. (2021). High-precision U-Pb zircon dating of late magmatism in the Samail ophiolite: A record of subduction initiation. Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth 126, e2020JB020758. https://doi.org/10.1029/2020JB020758
conf: Coordinates are converted from the published grid reference of dated sample UAE180 [423702 2781090], assuming UTM zone 40N on the Nahrawan datum used by the BGS UAE mapping; the paper does not state the datum, and a WGS84 reading would place it about 0.4 km away (25.14385, 56.24303). Timeline is the span of the later magmatic sequence given in the source.

s: Largest exposure of the ophiolite's metamorphic sole in the UAE
te: Rocks baked under a sliding ocean floor
ta: صخور طُهيت تحت قاع محيط زاحف
se: Around Masafi lie rocks that were squeezed and heated as a slab of ocean floor slid over the edge of Arabia
sa: حول مسافي تنتشر صخور انضغطت وسخنت حين زحفت كتلة من قاع المحيط فوق حافة الجزيرة العربية
desc: The Masafi–Ghub area is the largest exposure of metamorphic rocks beneath the Semail ophiolite in the UAE, covering about 100 km². It consists of greenschist- to locally amphibolite-facies quartz–chlorite schists, metacherts and minor meta-carbonate and meta-volcanic rocks of the Masafi–Ismah Group. A quartz schist sample gave a rutile age of 94.1 ± 2.6 Ma, and garnet–diopside amphibolites in the Masafi area record about 800 ± 100 °C and 1.1 ± 0.2 GPa. Carbonatites in the underlying Jebel Hakimah Group have a zircon age of 103 ± 1 Ma.
sig: The window shows the hot metamorphic sole formed as the ophiolite began to move, and separates the Khor Fakkan and Aswad ophiolite blocks.
ex: Roberts et al. (2016); Goodenough et al. (2010)
refs: Roberts, N.M.W., Thomas, R.J. & Jacobs, J. (2016). Geochronological constraints on the metamorphic sole of the Semail ophiolite in the United Arab Emirates. Geoscience Frontiers 7, 609–619. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gsf.2015.12.003

Goodenough, K.M., Styles, M.T., Schofield, D., Thomas, R.J., Crowley, Q.C., Lilly, R.M., McKervey, J., Stephenson, D. & Carney, J.N. (2010). Architecture of the Oman–UAE ophiolite: evidence for a multi-phase magmatic history. Arabian Journal of Geosciences 3(4), 439–458. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12517-010-0177-3
conf: No published outcrop coordinate was found; coordinates are those of Masafi town (25°18′48″N, 56°9′46″E, gazetteer/Wikipedia), which the Fujairah–Ras Al Khaimah border runs through. The pressure–temperature estimate is Gnos (1998) as cited by Roberts et al. Timeline runs from the 103 Ma carbonatites to the 94.1 Ma rutile age.

n: Wadi Ham Fault Zone at Al Bithnah
na: نطاق صدع وادي حام عند البثنة
s: Major fault corridor between two blocks of the Semail ophiolite
dr: NW–SE fault zone in the Semail ophiolite
el: Separates the Khor Fakkan and Aswad blocks
te: The valley that splits the mountains
se: Wadi Ham follows a great break in the rocks that splits the mountains into two giant blocks of old ocean floor
sa: يسير وادي حام على امتداد كسر عظيم في الصخور يقسم الجبال إلى كتلتين هائلتين من قاع محيط قديم
desc: Wadi Ham runs from Masafi to Fujairah city and the Gulf of Oman, with the village of Al Bithnah on its route. The British Geological Survey mapped a north-west to south-east fault zone along it that bounds the southern side of the Khor Fakkan ophiolite block and separates it from the Aswad block. The Aswad block is about 70 km north–south and holds the most extensive network of younger gabbros in the UAE ophiolite. Layered gabbros near Bithnah are mostly horizontal to gently inclined.
sig: The fault zone is one of the main structural boundaries that divide the UAE part of the Semail ophiolite into separate blocks, and has long served as a mountain pass.
disc: Separates Khor Fakkan and Aswad blocks
Ancient route through the Hajar Mountains
refs: Goodenough, K.M., Styles, M.T., Schofield, D., Thomas, R.J., Crowley, Q.C., Lilly, R.M., McKervey, J., Stephenson, D. & Carney, J.N. (2010). Architecture of the Oman–UAE ophiolite: evidence for a multi-phase magmatic history. Arabian Journal of Geosciences 3(4), 439–458. https://doi.org/10.1007/s12517-010-0177-3

Heikal, M.T.S. (1999). Layering in gabbroid rocks from Semail ophiolite, United Arab Emirates: characterization, tectonic control on origin and orientation. JKAU: Earth Sciences 11, 33–58. https://cegmr.kau.edu.sa/Files/320/Researches/51287_21477.pdf
conf: No published coordinate for the fault zone was found; coordinates are those of Al Bithnah village (25°11′20″N, 56°13′58″E, gazetteer/Wikipedia), which lies on the Wadi Ham route. The sources do not date the faulting; the timeline start is the oldest dated ophiolite crust in Goodenough et al. (96.4 Ma) and is a broad estimate. Arabic name is a descriptive translation.

s: Neolithic ritual platform of dugong bones in the Umm Al Quwain lagoon
dr: Settlement c. 4748–3814 BC; dugong mound 3522–3226 BC (2σ)
el: More than 40 dugongs in a 10 m² mound
te: The island of the sea-cow shrine
se: On a small island, Stone Age fishers carefully stacked the skulls and bones of more than 40 dugongs into a sacred platform
sa: على جزيرة صغيرة رتّب صيادو العصر الحجري جماجم أكثر من 40 أطومًا وعظامها في منصة مقدسة
desc: Akab is a small island in Khor al-Beidah, the lagoon of Umm Al Quwain, first found in 1989 and excavated again in 2006–2008. Its Late Neolithic settlement is dated by radiocarbon to between about 4748 and 3814 BC. An ovoid mound of about 10 m² and 0.30–0.40 m high holds the remains of more than 40 dugongs, with mandibles forming a base and skulls aligned in rows, together with several hundred objects such as shell and soft-stone beads; it is dated to 3522–3226 BC. Fish bones from the site belong to 56 bony-fish species in 42 genera and 22 families.
sig: Described by its excavators as the oldest known ritual site associated with the dugong.
ex: Méry et al. (2009); Lidour et al. (2019)
refs: Méry, S., Charpentier, V., Auxiette, G. & Pelle, E. (2009). A dugong bone mound: the Neolithic ritual site on Akab in Umm al-Quwain, United Arab Emirates. Antiquity 83, 696–708. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/antiquity/article/dugong-bone-mound-the-neolithic-ritual-site-on-akab-in-umm-alquwain-united-arab-emirates/8DE1147214D7B1AF44E76082DA262099

Lidour, K., Béarez, P., Charpentier, V. & Méry, S. (2019). The Prehistoric Fisheries of Akab Island (United Arab Emirates): New Insights into Coastal Subsistence during Neolithic in Eastern Arabia. The Journal of Island and Coastal Archaeology. https://doi.org/10.1080/15564894.2018.1531330
conf: Coordinates are from Lidour et al. (2019), whose text lost its degree symbols; read as 25°34′09.94″N, 55°34′31.67″E, which agrees within about 3 km with the gazetteer point for Akab Island. Timeline years are converted from the calibrated BC dates. Wikipedia gives the Arabic name as جزيرة الأكعاب; عكاب is the common local spelling.

n: Umm Al Quwain spit and lagoon system
na: لسان أم القيوين الرملي ونظامه الساحلي
s: Holocene sand spit and barrier lagoon shaped by sea-level change
dr: Sea level about 2 m higher around 5,500 BP
te: A town on a ribbon of sand
se: Umm Al Quwain sits on a long finger of sand that waves and tides built up as the sea rose and fell over thousands of years
sa: تقوم أم القيوين على لسان طويل من الرمل بنته الأمواج والمدّ والجزر مع ارتفاع البحر وانخفاضه عبر آلاف السنين
desc: The city of Umm Al Quwain is built on a coastal dune system along the main spit that encloses Khor al-Beidah, a lagoon about 20 km long, 8 km wide and about 127 km² in area. Sea level stood about 2 m higher than today around 5,500 BP and about 1.5 m higher around 4,500 BP; the lagoon reached its maximum extent around 3,500 BP, the southern ridge was breached around 2,600 BP and a ridge nearly closed the lagoon by about 1,500 BP. About 8 km² was reclaimed between 1965 and 1984, and grey mangrove cover has expanded since 1984 as dredging improved tidal flushing.
sig: A spit and barrier-lagoon system on the Arabian Gulf coast that records Holocene sea-level change and modern human impact.
disc: Sea level about 2 m higher at 5,500 BP
refs: Forti, L., Degli Esposti, M., Cremaschi, M., Borgi, F., Azzoni, R.S. & Zerboni, A. (2024). Geomorphological evolution of the Umm al-Quwain (UAE) coastal-lagoon system: Natural processes and recent human impact. Catena 247, 108517. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.catena.2024.108517
conf: Coordinates are those of Umm Al Quwain city (25°33′12″N, 55°32′51″E, gazetteer/Wikipedia), which stands on the spit; the source gives no point coordinates. The Holocene sea-level and lagoon dates are from Bernier et al. (1995) as summarised by Forti et al.; timeline starts at the 5,500 BP highstand. Arabic name is a descriptive translation.
